statement: Do there exist 2018 distinct positive integers such that the sum of their squares is a perfect cube and the sum of their cubes is a perfect square?

$P$ is outside circle $\Gamma$; $PA$ is tangent at $A$. Line $\ell$ through $P$ meets $\Gamma$ at $B$, $C$ ($B$ between $P$ and $C$). $D$ is the reflection of $B$ over $P$. $\omega_1$ is the circumcircle of $\triangle DAC$; $\omega_2$ of $\triangle PAB$. They meet again at $E \neq A$. Line $EB$ meets $\omega_1$ again at $F$. Prove $CF = AB$.

Find all triples $\{a,b,c\}$ of coprime (but not necessarily pairwise coprime) positive integers such that $a + b + c$ divides $a^{12}+b^{12}+c^{12}$, $a^{23}+b^{23}+c^{23}$, and $a^{11004}+b^{11004}+c^{11004}$.

Acute $\triangle ABC$ with $AC > AB$; $\Gamma$ = circumcircle; $D$ = midpoint of minor arc $BC$. $E \in AB$, $F \in AC$ with $AE = AF$. $P \neq A$ = second intersection of circumcircle of $\triangle AEF$ with $\Gamma$. $G = PE \cap \Gamma$, $H = PF \cap \Gamma$; $J = DG \cap AB$, $K = DH \cap AC$. Show line $JK$ passes through the midpoint of $BC$.
Find all $n$-tuples $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ of distinct positive integers such that $\dfrac{(a_1+d)(a_2+d)\cdots(a_n+d)}{a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n}$ is an integer for every integer $d \geq 0$.
A company has $n$ employees; each works at least one of 7 days (except one who works none). Any two employees differ on at least 3 days (one works when the other doesn't). Find the maximum $n$.
